name: Soft half-volley resets from the feet
summary: Alone at a wall, feed a low ball that bounces at your feet and reset it with a short half-volley between a net line and a low-reset line, as in the transition zone.
setup: Tape a line on the wall about 0.9 m above the floor (the net) and a second line about 1.3 m (the top of a low reset); stand about 4 m from the wall
Hit a soft, low ball at the wall just above the net line so the rebound comes back low and bounces at or just in front of your feet
Bend your knees, keep the paddle face open and in front, and play a short half-volley straight off the bounce so it hits the wall between the two lines
A reset counts when it lands between the lines; above the top line, below the net line or a miss is an error. Sets of 10
success_criterion: In each of 3 sets of 10 half-volleys, at least 7 resets land between the two lines
safety_notes: Soft feeds only: the pressure in this drill is a low ball at the feet, not pace, so never drive the feed. Bend the knees, not the back, and keep the paddle in front. Stop if your knees or back hurt.
coach_rationale: (judgment) Many errors under pressure (AN-07 forced-error share) come from balls landing at the feet in the transition zone, where there is no time for a full stroke. A soft feed that bounces at the feet rehearses the short half-volley reset without the fast rebound of drive-and-block drills, alone at a wall.
